old: **The collection of cosignatures for an event its protocol has not yet admitted** (registered under CC 3.1.7 R2(a); the hold of [CC 3.3.4](part_3_the_namespace.md), general to any cosigned row of [CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md)): `{state}` ∈ `pending` \| `signature` — closed; wire `cosign:pending:v1`, `cosign:signature:v1`. A **pending** row carries a cosignable event whole, as its typed door takes it, less its cosignatures: the event, its primary signer and, as its own statement, the primary's signature over the event's signing bytes. It is named by the event's **quorum key**, sha256(`ciris-persist/cosign-pending/v1` ‖ JCS(the event with no signature in it)): the digest of what every signer signs, covering no signature, so it is equal on every node whatever signature bytes that node holds. It is admitted only if the primary's signature verifies and the primary resolves to an active member of the group at the event's signed instant. That instant is the signer's to choose, so it is bounded as [CC 3.3.6.3](#3.3.6.3) bounds an owner act: a pending row whose primary is no longer an active member at receipt is refused `asserted_at_stale` once its signed instant is older than the freshness window W ([CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md)). One is open per proposer per group; only the primary's node mints it, every other holder carries its bytes verbatim, and a re-wrap is refused. A **signature** row carries the quorum key, the signer's key id and that signer's hybrid signature over the same signing bytes the primary signed, which is exactly one `additional_scrubs` entry ([CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md)); its id is sha256(`ciris-persist/cosign-signature/v1` ‖ quorum key ‖ signer key id). It is admitted only if both halves verify against the pending event's bytes and the signer is an active member at the event's signed instant, under the same bound on a signer that has since left; a second signature by the same signer over the same event settles as already held and is no conflict. **Neither row is the event.** Nothing folds from them and no seat moves on them; when the signatures a node holds satisfy the group's `consensus_protocol`, the event lands through its own typed door with their union as its cosignatures. The landed act is named by the same quorum key: replication offers and settles it by that key, and a row that names the act, a cosigned `withdraws` first of all ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) rule 0), resolves on every node that holds it, whichever sufficient set that node assembled. **Audience:** the members who were active at the event's signed instant and are members still when served, and no one else, in a group of any kind; a member removed since is served nothing, the invitee of a pending widening is not among them, and the member a pending removal names is a member and is served. **Withdrawal:** the proposer's `withdraws` of the pending row ends its holding and serving. **Holding ends once:** a node that has dropped a pending row, at its window's end or on its withdrawal, does not hold that row again, and no node begins to hold one whose event was signed more than one hold window before the row reached it, so no node holds a change later than two windows after its signed instant; a proposer that still wants the change signs it anew. A signature row is never withdrawn: a member that has sent its signature cannot recall it, and an event assembled from signatures that satisfy the protocol is judged by its door on those signatures alone. Under [CC 2.6.1.8](part_2_the_grammar.md) a signature row is the per-signer statement and the quorum key takes that subsection's form; the collection is the same.

old: One row per evidence blob of a registered suite; the blob is a Commons blob named in `evidence_refs` by its SHA-256, and `{prefix}` is that digest's first 16 lowercase hex characters. `{suite}` ∈ `safety_battery` — a closed vocabulary: a new suite is admitted by registration as a new value and states its own kind set, cell form and what its pass ratio counts. For `safety_battery`, `{kind}` ∈ `capture` \| `interpret`: a **capture** is the question-and-answer pairs for one `{cell}` (a language and a domain, as `ru_mental_health`) against one agent version and one model, with its CI provenance; an **interpret** is a judge's per-criterion verdicts over the capture of the same `{prefix}`, the blob citing the rubric's id, version and hash and the judge model and prompt hash. Because the capture's digest is in the dimension, a re-post of the same capture is a `supersedes` and never a silent replace. `score` is 1.0 for a capture and 2·(pass ratio) − 1 for an interpret, so every criterion failed is −1 and every criterion passed is +1. An evidence row may name the Goal-side row it is offered against in `references_attestation_id` (a `goal:{scale}`, `approach:{goal_id}` or `method:{approach_id}:{substrate_rung}` row, [CC 3.1.9.7](#3.1.9.7)); the door refuses a reference that does not resolve to a live row of those families (`evidence_reference_unresolved`, whatever the cause: no such row, another family, or withdrawn) and admits a row with no reference; what counts as progress is the Goal side's `progress_measure:{method_id}` whose `evidence_refs` cite the evidence, never the worker's reference alone. A `withdraws` / `recants` is a **boundary, not a deletion**: the latest admitted revocation's `asserted_at` is `R`, and every grant with `asserted_at ≤ R` is out of the fold, whichever row the revocation named — so revoking the newest grant never resurrects an older one. Among the grants after `R` (all of them, if there is no revocation), the latest `asserted_at` wins, ties on the smallest attestation id; no grant means no consent. A revocation is therefore a **hard stop** no configuration overrides, and capture resumes only on a **fresh** grant asserted after `R` from the owner-binding chain. **The grant MAY be authored by the node's owner:** attester = the owner — a live roster key of the owner's fedID ([CC 3.3.6.3](#3.3.6.3)) at the grant's `asserted_at` — and attested = the node whose traces are at issue, which is what scopes the grant; `subject_key_ids[]` names all three parties: the node, the key that was the node's owner at `asserted_at`, and the agent key that acts on the node. The node-authored form stays valid, and the fold below groups both forms by `attested_key_id`. Each named party may withdraw ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) rule 2); only the attester recants ([CC 2.4.1.3](part_2_the_grammar.md)), so under owner authorship the person holds recant and under node authorship only withdrawal — trace-sharing consent is the person's act, as [CC 3.3.6](#3.3.6) and `consent:replication` already have it. **Four readings the consent-plane model (pinned by the register) fixes:** a new owner's revocation door is this fold's and no other — its own grant or revocation as the later row, never the old owner's seat; the agent key's withdrawal is folded like the owner's, a boundary `R`, and what a boundary excludes is grants only, never the traces already captured while a grant was live (the record stands, [CC 1.13.6](part_1_foundation.md)); `consent:state:*` rows on one subject use the same boundary fold, the latest admitted revocation's `asserted_at` putting every earlier grant out; and a decay protocol that began under a grant runs to `complete` after a fresh grant is made — the fresh grant covers capture from its own `asserted_at` and resurrects nothing the decay removed. **Revocation authority (normative):** the node's owner MUST always be able to revoke. A grant the node emits for itself MUST list, in `subject_key_ids[]`, the key that was its owner **at the grant's own `asserted_at`** — `owner_of(node)` resolved at that instant over the owner-binding rows ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)), never the receiver's current view, so a later ownership transfer neither admits nor un-admits a grant already made and every peer reaches the same verdict once the binding rows have replicated (a grant whose binding rows have not yet arrived is held, as every owner-gated row is). A new owner does not inherit the old owner's revocation seat — it asks the node to re-grant, or emits its own grant, which the fold prefers as the later row. A grant or revocation from a key that was neither the node nor its owner at the row's `asserted_at` is not this node's consent and MUST NOT be folded as one.
